title: Singleton and Builder
idea: Singleton guarantees one shared instance of a class with one access point. Builder assembles a complex object step by step, then checks and freezes it.
points: A Singleton creates its instance on first request and returns it ever after.
A module exporting one instance acts as a Singleton: Node loads each file once.
A Builder collects options through chained methods that each return `this`.
`build()` validates required parts once, then returns a finished, frozen object.

steps.caption: The class exists, but its private static `#instance` is still `null`. No object has been made.
The first `get()` finds `#instance` empty, so it creates the one `Config` object and stores it.
The second `get()` skips creation and returns the stored object.
`a` and `b` hold the same reference, so `a === b` is `true`.

code.title: A guarded Singleton
code.caption: Every `Counter.get()` returns the same object, so hits add up. A direct `new` after the first `get()` is refused; one that runs earlier would still slip through.

walk.text: One private static slot for the instance, and private state inside it.
The constructor refuses a second object once the first exists.
`??=` creates the instance only on the first call.
Two calls share one counter; `new Counter()` now throws.

code.title: A fluent Builder
code.caption: Add a `note(text)` step to the builder. The `Order` class does not change.

walk.text: `Order` is the product. `Object.freeze` is shallow, so `build()` also freezes the items array.
The builder keeps parts in a private draft with safe defaults.
Each step sets one part and returns `this`, so calls chain.
`build()` checks required parts once, then copies and freezes the array, so the builder cannot leak edits.
Readable construction: each call names what it sets.
A missing customer fails at build time with a clear message.

pitfalls: A Singleton is global state; inject it into classes so tests can pass a fake.
Skip the Builder when an options object with defaults reads clearly enough.
Validate in `build()`, not in each step, or the order of calls starts to matter.

quiz.why: `get` builds the object once and returns it every time, so both increments hit it. `make()` builds a fresh object with `n` at 0.

takeaway: Singleton shares one object; Builder assembles one carefully, then freezes it.
